newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi clarifies remarks on EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi clarifies remarks on EMU delay.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi rules out any assumption of delays to the timetable for Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU), his spokesman Francesco Luna said on Friday.

Luna telephoned news agencies to clarify the Italian position after Prodi said in response to a question during a pre-recorded television show that a German request to delay the start of EMU, planned for 1999, was "possible".
"The Prime Minister excludes that there is any assumption of a delay to the timetable for a single European currency," Luna said.
He said this position had been "clearly expressed" during a telephone conversation Prodi had with French President Jacques Chirac about EMU on Thursday.

Problems faced by almost all European states in reining in their budget deficits to bring them under the threshold laid down in the Maastricht Treaty has led many economists to increase the probability rating of a delay in the start.

Prodi was asked during the TV recording if he thought Germany, rather than Italy, could seek a delay. "That is their business. It is also possible. We must be ready...We cannot allow ourselves to ask for a delay," he said.
